\chapter{Software Requirements}
\section{User Interactions / Use Cases}
FlakeTrace has two actors. A \textbf{Developer} invokes it directly against a failing test
they are investigating. A \textbf{CI Pipeline} invokes it the same way, on demand for a known
failing test rather than on every build --- Non-Functional Requirement NFR-1 (Section
\ref{ch4:sec:nfr}) is the reason: our stakeholders' own CI-time budgets rule out running it on
every successful build. Both actors drive the same seven use cases (Figure
\ref{ch4:fig:usecases}): submit a diagnosis request, through to receiving a typed certificate.

\section{Non-Functional Requirements}\label{ch4:sec:nfr}

\subsection{Reliability}
A \textbf{Verified} certificate requires $\geq 18$ of 20 matching clean replays \emph{and} a
Wilson 95\% lower bound $\geq 0.70$ on the reproduction rate --- both figures are stated in
\texttt{docs/03-Design/certificate-contract.md} and implemented as the literal default
threshold in \texttt{eval/outcome.py} (\texttt{DEFAULT\_LOWER\_BOUND\_THRESHOLD = 0.70}). The
Wilson estimator itself is tested against \texttt{statsmodels} (\texttt{eval/tests/
test\_stats.py}), not just asserted. We never report a single numeric confidence score ---
reliability is always \emph{matching failures out of $N$ replays plus an interval}, per the
certificate contract.

The \textbf{non-perturbation control} (execute the passing and failing order, each
uninstrumented and instrumented, requiring all four outcomes to match before any measurement is
accepted) is \textbf{not yet implemented as a dedicated, automated check} in Iteration 1. It
remains a committed requirement, not a dropped one: our own N2 timezone-sensitivity defect
(\texttt{docs/evidence-m3.md}) is exactly the kind of self-inflicted-failure risk this control
exists to catch, found instead by manual cross-platform re-measurement.

\subsection{Instrumentation Overhead (NFR-1)}
\todo{M3: no overhead threshold exists yet, deliberately -- \texttt{non-functional.md} states
this explicitly rather than inventing a number before it is measured. Iteration 1's evidence
collection is static-only (\texttt{javap} bytecode reads, no code is instrumented or executed
differently because of FlakeTrace), so there is no runtime overhead to measure yet: this NFR
becomes testable once Iteration 2 adds runtime instrumentation, if static evidence proves
insufficient (\texttt{docs/03-Design/decisions/ADR-001-iteration1-evidence-without-
instrumentation.md}). The envelope from stakeholder interviews (5--15 min PR-CI tolerance,
SH1; 30 min opt-in, SH3) is recorded as context, not a current measurement.}

\subsection{Security and Usability}
\textbf{Security.} \texttt{non-functional.md}'s security requirements (rootless containers, no
network during test execution, resource limits, redaction) describe the \textbf{committed,
containerised Iteration-1-and-beyond runtime} --- checked against the real code
(\texttt{grep -rn "redact\textbackslash{}|rootless\textbackslash{}|sandbox" runner/ evidence/
eval/}), none of it exists yet: Iteration 1 runs tests as a native JVM process
(\texttt{runner/order\_runner.py}), not inside any container. This is a real, stated gap, not a
silent one: every real diagnosis still runs real project code locally, so the committed
sandboxing work is squarely FYP-2 scope, named on the cut list in
\texttt{docs/02-Requirements/scope-boundary.md} if the team is behind at Final-1.

\textbf{Usability.} The proposal's brief described four generic abstention reasons (unsupported
resource, budget exhausted, unstable build, inconsistent outcomes --- \texttt{docs/03-Design/
certificate-contract.md}). What Iteration 1 actually built in \texttt{eval/outcome.py} is a
\textbf{richer, different} typed-reason enum with six reasons the decision table can actually
emit (\texttt{VICTIM\_FAILS\_ALONE}, \texttt{NOT\_REPRODUCED}, \texttt{SIGNATURE\_MISMATCH},
\texttt{INFRASTRUCTURE\_FAILURE}, \texttt{NO\_SUPPORTED\_RESOURCE\_EVIDENCE},
\texttt{SOURCE\_INTEGRITY\_FAILED}) plus one reserved for forward compatibility
(\texttt{BELOW\_CONFIDENCE\_THRESHOLD}, never emitted --- \texttt{CANDIDATE} is used instead,
a team decision recorded in \texttt{docs/contracts/report-schema.md}). This is a deliberate
scope change from the proposal, not a drift we are hiding: every reason still maps to a
different, concrete next action for the developer, which was the brief's actual usability
requirement.

\section{Acceptance Criteria}
Table \ref{ch4:tab:acceptance} reproduces the project's success criteria (\texttt{docs/02-
Requirements/non-functional.md}, Q71) with an honest Iteration-1 status against each one ---
some are met structurally by how \texttt{eval/outcome.py} is written, others are genuinely
unmeasured yet.

\begin{longtable}{p{4.3cm}p{3.6cm}p{5.8cm}}
\caption{Success criteria and Iteration-1 status}\label{ch4:tab:acceptance}\\
\toprule
\textbf{Criterion} & \textbf{Target} & \textbf{Iteration-1 Status} \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
\textbf{Criterion} & \textbf{Target} & \textbf{Iteration-1 Status} \\
\midrule
\endhead
Verified threshold & $\geq 18/20$ replays, Wilson lower bound $\geq 0.70$ & \textbf{Met by
  construction.} \texttt{decide()} cannot reach \texttt{VERIFIED} any other way; tested in
  \texttt{eval/tests/test\_outcome.py}. \\
Deletion checks & Every Verified sequence passes 1-minimality & \textbf{Met.} \texttt{ddmin}
  (ADR-007) guarantees this for every multi-polluter case; real F3 case confirms it. \\
Explanation & Every Verified explanation includes a test$\to$resource$\to$test path &
  \textbf{Met by construction.} \texttt{decide()} requires a non-null resource edge before
  \texttt{VERIFIED} is reachable. \\
Controls & No false confident diagnosis on non-OD controls & \textbf{Partially measured.} All
  3 negative controls in the fixture (N1, N2, N3) correctly abstain, never \texttt{VERIFIED}
  (\texttt{fixtures/od-fixture/ground\_truth.json}). Not yet measured on a larger corpus. \\
Cost reduction vs.\ baseline ($\geq 25\%$ lower median invocations) & $\geq 25\%$ & \textbf{Open
  --- claim B11.} Our own random-order baseline now runs for real on F1--F4 (found the bug in
  1--3 shuffles every trial); published-tool comparators (iFixFlakies, iDFlakies) are not yet
  integrated, so the rigorous paired comparison this criterion requires is not yet possible. \\
Success-at-budget ($\leq 5$pp lower, paired CIs) & $\leq 5$pp & \textbf{Open --- same claim
  B11 gap.} \\
Instrumentation overhead & Below a stakeholder-accepted threshold & \textbf{Open, no number
  yet} --- see NFR-1 (Section \ref{ch4:sec:nfr}). \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
